key_insight: Aggregate validation metrics like perplexity can follow smooth power laws while individual downstream tasks show heterogeneous scaling — some improve, some plateau, and some worsen — so validation perplexity alone is an unreliable predictor of task performance as models scale.
problem_solved: Clarifies why using aggregate scaling laws (validation loss/perplexity) to predict downstream task performance fails, and identifies the mechanisms (token-level averaging and lack of a universal parametric mapping) behind that failure.
method: Empirical, task-level scaling study: measure downstream performance across model sizes and compute budgets to reveal diverse per-task trajectories (monotonic improvement, plateaus, degradation).
Diagnostic decomposition: analyze token-level losses and their aggregation to show how averaging obscures task-relevant signal.
Statistical assessment: evaluate parametric fits linking perplexity to downstream metrics and demonstrate that no simple family robustly generalizes across tasks.
impact: Practitioners should not rely solely on validation perplexity when forecasting gains from scaling; instead, evaluate task-specific metrics and consider token-level or task-aware extrapolations to guide compute allocation and model selection.
visual_elements: Line chart: aggregate validation loss (smooth power-law) overlaid with multiple downstream-task curves showing improvement, plateau, and degradation.
Heatmap or raster: token-level loss contributions across inputs to illustrate how averaging masks signal.
Scatter plot: validation perplexity vs. downstream task performance showing weak/variable correlation and poor predictive fit.
Flowchart/Checklist: recommended evaluation workflow — task-specific metrics, token-level diagnostics, and non-parametric/task-aware extrapolation.
paper_authors: Michael Y. Hu, Jane Pan, Ayush Rajesh Jhaveri, Nicholas Lourie, Kyunghyun Cho
